publication.subtitle: Open Access Modelling of the ASEAN Power Grid with TZ-APG
author: Vu, T.
Shivakumar, A.
Suarez, I.
Puspitarini, H. D.
Majid, A.

description: ASEAN power model with significant new regional transmission infrastructure.
pathwayDescription:
The Regional Interconnection (REGI) scenario marks the first major structural expansion of the ASEAN Power Grid in TransitionZero’s set of TZ-APG v1 pathways. It introduces new cross-border transmission projects identified under the ASEAN Interconnection Masterplan Study (AIMS III), including 18 interconnectors across the region and two additional subsea cables linking Singapore with Vietnam and Cambodia. These additions represent the backbone of a future interconnected ASEAN electricity market.

While the model includes extensive new interconnection routes, the system-wide generation capacity and mix in 2035 remain nearly identical to BAU and EBAU. This reflects the TZ-APG model’s design emphasis on grid utilization and trade optimization rather than differential technology uptake. The scenario thus focuses on regional power flow patterns, investment costs, and trade efficiency rather than major shifts in generation technology.

The pathway demonstrates how regional coordination enhances flexibility, allowing countries to leverage resource complementarities. Integration also improves system utilization, reduces stranded-capacity risk, and slightly lowers system costs by avoiding redundant investment in domestic gas and storage. It reflects an ASEAN energy system beginning to function as a shared market rather than as a set of isolated national grids.

coreDrivers.policies: Target technology shares: minimum RE/solar shares for Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines are imposed as constraints. Target capacity levels: minimum hydro, solar, RE and wind capacities (Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Singapore, Viet Nam) and coal caps (Myanmar, Viet Nam) are imposed, several binding exactly in 2035. The policy set is identical to BAU; new links let constraint-driven RE in one country (e.g. Kalimantan hydro) displace gas elsewhere, notably in the Philippines.
coreDrivers.emissionsTargets: Absolute emissions caps are imposed as model constraints: Indonesia's power emissions peak at 290 MtCO2eq by 2030 and Singapore's at 60 MtCO2eq in 2030. In REGI's 2035 results Indonesia emits 240.9 Mt and Singapore 23.2 Mt, so neither cap binds at the reported year.
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: Least-cost optimisation weighs new subsea and overland HVDC interconnectors (higher cost per km for subsea) against domestic storage and gas, using DEA catalogue capex/O&M. With USD 121.89bn of transmission, cheap Kalimantan and Lao hydro displaces gas, cutting Philippine gas capacity from 7.5 to 4.2 GW and ASEAN storage to 43.5 GW. ASEAN system cost falls to 88.47bn (−2.3% vs BAU).
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: Electricity demand growth is an exogenous driver common to all four TZ-APG pathways and does not differentiate them: country CAGRs for 2023-2035 range from 1.6% (Myanmar) to 8.1% (Cambodia). Sources are national plans (Cambodia PDMP, Indonesia JETP CIPP, Philippines PDP, Singapore Energy 2050 Committee, Thailand PDP, Viet Nam PDP) and, for Brunei, Lao PDR, Malaysia and Myanmar, TransitionZero estimates based on historical trends and World Bank, IMF and IIASA population and GDP projections.
coreDrivers.otherDrivers: Grid topology: REGI adds the remaining AIMS III interconnectors and Singapore's links to Viet Nam and Cambodia (54 routes), assumed built by 2035. New subsea links such as Sabah→Luzon (3,648 MW, 20.0 TWh) and Kalimantan→Sabah (3,892 MW, 18.5 TWh) create the Borneo–Philippines 'green lane', reducing ASEAN storage to 43.5 GW and gas to 129.5 GW. The assumption is infrastructure design, not any of the other named drivers.

dependencies.dependency_description: Beyond national targets, REGI assumes the full AIMS III programme and Singapore's import links are built by 2035. The pathway depends on regional frameworks the report describes as still under development: the renewed APG MOU, phase 3 of AIMS III, BIMP-PIP and Singapore's import-diversification strategy. The report presents BIMP-PIP and Malaysia's ENEGEM exchange as policy steps aligned with the modelled Kalimantan–Sabah–Luzon corridor.

REGI's multilateral flows, including wheeling through Sabah to Luzon and through Malaysia to Singapore, require multilateral trading arrangements, harmonised grid codes and technical standards that the report says still need to be developed. The report also calls for a common green-electricity tracking framework to manage carbon leakage. Export, wheeling and import charges are not represented in v1, so their regulatory design is an unmodelled condition behind the trade volumes shown.

Transmission capex more than doubles to about USD 122bn for a 2.3% system-cost saving (USD 90.5bn → 88.47bn). The pathway depends on capital for long-lived, mostly subsea HVDC assets such as Sabah–Luzon (USD 23.5bn) and Sumatera–Singapore (USD 18.3bn). The report flags low-utilisation risk for Singapore's cables to Cambodia and Viet Nam (0.2 and 0.5 TWh) and says export, wheeling and import costs need better representation.

With wider integration, emissions rise in more exporting nodes (Lao PDR 10.4 Mt and Thailand 108.7 Mt, versus 0.6 and 104.9 Mt in BAU). The report warns that uneven impacts on exporting communities and carbon-leakage risk require a common green-electricity tracking framework. It also states that political and social buy-in depends on transparent data.

Client demand for clean electricity and its traceability is the report's case for green corridors such as Kalimantan–Sabah–Luzon (20.0 TWh into Luzon). The report gives no willingness-to-pay or behavioural assumption, so this is context rather than a constraint.

REGI rests on building the rest of AIMS III plus the Singapore links by 2035, which the annex assumes rather than assesses. New subsea HVDC routes carry the main shifts: Sabah→Luzon (3,648 MW, 20.0 TWh) replaces Philippine gas (7.5 → 4.2 GW), alongside Kalimantan→Sabah (3,892 MW, 18.5 TWh) and Sumatera→Singapore (3,664 MW, 6.6 TWh). Storage falls to 43.5 GW.
Storage falls to 43.5 GW (up to 36% below BAU), concentrated in Viet Nam (35.4 GW). Regional interconnection substitutes for BESS in Indonesia (1.3 GW) and Malaysia (2.5 GW).

REGI's 'green lane' relies on Kalimantan hydropower (7.4 GW, 39.5 TWh) for export to Sabah and Luzon, and on Lao hydro (94.2 TWh) for Viet Nam. Singapore diversifies imports to Sumatera (6.6 TWh), Peninsular Malaysia, Cambodia and Viet Nam because its own resources are limited.

byMetric.scopeLimitations: Derived: node emissions ÷ node generation, 2035 (ASEAN 0.397 t/MWh). Generation-based, excludes imports. Gas basket and emissions scope not stated (report labels MtCO2eq). Grid-to-grid node model; plant data omits most rooftop/small-scale solar; no captive series.

Total power-system emissions by node, Mt, 2035 (ASEAN 829.4 Mt). GHG basket and emissions scope not stated; report charts label MtCO2eq. Grid-to-grid node model; plant data omits most rooftop/small-scale solar; no captive series.

Installed MW by node and technology, 2035. Storage = lithium-ion battery, separate column, MW only (no MWh). Pumped-storage hydro is included in hydropower, not separated. Coal limited to plants operating or under construction in 2023. Plant data omits most rooftop/small-scale solar; no captive series.

Annual GWh by node and technology, 2035 (ASEAN 2,088.4 TWh). Generation within each node; imports/exports shown separately in transmission trade. Plant data omits most rooftop/small-scale solar; no captive series.
Derived from generation by technology (share of node/country/ASEAN total), 2035. Same on-grid boundary as Generation; excludes imported electricity from the mix of the importing country.

Line-level trade (GWh), capacity (MW) and capex (USD bn) between the 24 nodes. 54 routes incl. new AIMS III and Singapore links; capacity optimised; capex for upgrades and new build vs BAU. Lines act as combined interfaces between node centre-points; HVAC/HVDC by distance; no distribution grid; no trade with China; no wheeling charges.

Capital (USD/MW), fixed O&M (USD/MW-yr), variable (USD/MWh) and fuel (USD/MWh) costs per country and technology, incl. Li-ion battery and HVAC/HVDC/subsea transmission. DEA Viet Nam/Indonesia average applied to all countries; single ASEAN fuel prices.

granularity: By sector, part of value chain
byMetric.scopeLimitations: Systems cost by node = generator capex 2023-2035 plus 2035 opex (USD bn); blends capex with one year of opex. Transmission capex by line vs BAU (total USD 121.89bn). No technology split of generation capex.

Static technical lifetimes (coal 30 yr, gas and oil 40 yr, hydro 50 yr, solar 25 yr, wind 27 yr). No early-retirement constraint; coal capacity identical across all four pathways (101.8 GW in 2035 vs 98.4 GW in 2023 incl. under-construction plants).
